name: Zapier
summary: Zapier connects your app to thousands of other apps with no-code workflows called Zaps, run on Zapier's own servers.

free_plan_covers.note: The Free plan gives 100 tasks a month and only two-step Zaps (one trigger, one action), and it can't use Webhooks, so your app can't start a Zap on it. Enough to try Zapier, not to run an app.

first_paid_usd_month.note: The Professional plan is $29.99 a month billed monthly ($19.99 a month billed yearly) for 750 tasks. More tasks cost more.

portability.note: Zaps are built in Zapier's editor from Zapier's own app connections and only run on Zapier, so moving away means rebuilding each one somewhere else.

self_hostable.note: Every plan on the pricing page is hosted by Zapier; there is no version you can run on your own server.

code_steps.note: Code by Zapier runs JavaScript or Python in a step. The Free plan allows 1 second of run time per step and Professional allows 30 seconds; outside npm packages need a paid plan.

webhook_triggers.note: The Catch Hook trigger in Webhooks by Zapier gives a Zap a web address your app can send data to. It needs a paid plan (Professional or higher).

setup.step: Create a Zapier account and pick a Professional plan, since webhook triggers aren't on the Free plan.
Make a Zap that starts with Webhooks by Zapier, Catch Hook, and copy the webhook address into your app's environment file.

builder_notes: POST to the Zapier webhook from server code, reading the address from ZAPIER_WEBHOOK_URL; anyone who has the address can start the Zap.
Every action step in a Zap counts as a task, so send one webhook per event instead of one per field or item.
